subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool contract, and what raw-media egress, fallback, provider capability, config, and session/audit policy should govern that path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution changes sensitive local media forwarding, model capability routing, provider serialization, and session transcript semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, model/provider capability routing, explicit raw-media egress, payload limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep audio transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of the read tool and direct users to existing STT/media-understanding paths until maintainers are ready to own native audio egress.

options.title: Fold into broader native-audio design
options.body: Treat this read-tool request as a subcase of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 if maintainers want one product design thread for native audio input.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, model/provider capability routing, explicit raw-media egress, payload limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across read-tool, media-understanding, inbound attachment, and product/security boundary surfaces involved in this decision.
